## Installation

First, install the quarto extension

<!--- below is desired installation path, TBD on implementation --->

`quarto add quarto-graph`

Then install the python package, which is used to resolve graph data:

```sh
uv add quarto-graph
```

## Add to `_quarto.yml`

To enable the extension in your quarto website, change the project type to 
`quarto-graph` and add it to the `filters`:

```yaml
project:
  type: quarto-graph

filters:
  - quarto-graph
```

## Using Wikilinks

This extension enables wikilink syntax, a way to connect internal pages in your 
project using a `[[`. Wikilinks can be a convenient way to refer to pages 
without explicitly knowing and reference their file path. The way this works is
by adding an *alias* to individual pages using the `also-known-as` frontmatter
key:

For example, if we want to refer to the homepage of our website by "Home", we 
can write in `/index.qmd`:

```markdown
---
title: quarto-graph
also-known-as: Home
---
```

And then connect it to another page by referencing "Home" with a wikilink in that 
page. e.g.

*some-other-page/index.qmd*:

```markdown
Go back to [[Home]] using this wikilink
```

Additionally, this extension enables regular markdown links to also be 
connected. For example, these are equivalent:

- `[[Home]]`
- `[Home](index.qmd)`

See [[Wikilinks and Aliases]] for the full linking syntax.

## Graphs in your website

After building connections between pages, you can embed a graph, and you can 
autogenerating backlinks.

1. The extension provides a pre-built Graph widget which can be inserted on any 
page as a shortcode:

`{{{< quarto-graph-full >}}}`

{{< quarto-graph-full >}}

See [[The Graph Widget]] for more about the graph widget, how to embed it in 
pages, and how to customize it.

## Render

<!--- not sure if this section is needed --->

A wikilink resolves live, at render time, against every other page in the
project. Nothing rewrites your `.qmd` source, ever. 

## Frontmatter reference

| Key | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `title:` | Page title, and the link text shown when a wikilink has no `\|display` override |
| `type:` | Colors the node in the graph widget: `concept`, `person`, `reference`, `project`, `experiment`, `moc`; anything else (or omitted) falls back to gray |
| `also-known-as:` | Extra names this page's wikilinks can be reached by, on top of its filename. A separate key from Quarto's own `aliases:`; see [[Wikilinks and Aliases]] for why |
